transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-06 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Recordings: enabled
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood CSM), Priya Rao (NovaEdge CTO), Ben Torres (NovaEdge Eng Mgr), Aisha Malik (NovaEdge Data Platform)

Auto Summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect):
- Usage up 37% q/q driven by support chat and product recommendations
- Cost per 1M tokens increased due to longer contexts and fewer cached prefixes
- One P1 incident in Feb due to autoscaler misconfig + region failover; mitigations planned
- NovaEdge interested in Dedicated reserved capacity pilot and SOC2/ISO copy for procurement

Topics:
1) Usage trends and cost breakdown
2) Reliability incident review
3) Performance (latency/throughput) and Dedicated pilot discussion
4) Security/compliance requests and procurement timeline
5) Next steps and owners

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Maya: alright hi everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, i'll hand over to Liam to kick off the qbr, yeah
[00:08] Liam: hey thanks Maya, Priya, Ben, Aisha good to see you all, quick agenda, we'll run through usage, costs, incident recap, then roadmap and next steps
[00:18] Priya: works for me, trying to keep this tight, we have a budget review next week so would love the numbers
[00:22] Ben: yea same, and also the infra team wants to know whether Dedicated actually moves the needle on p50 latency
[00:30] Liam: cool, starting with usage - overall calls up about 37% quarter over quarter, embeddings steady but text gen higher driven by support bot and recs, average session length now 1.8k tokens vs 1.2k previous
[00:45] Aisha: is that total token count or per-call?
[00:48] Liam: total token count; per-call is up because we extended context windows on the support flows, so cache hit rate dropped to ~22% from 45%
[01:00] Priya: 22% cache hit is rough, what's suggested to improve?
[01:04] Maya: a few levers: smarter prefix caching (we noticed some prefix churn), smaller context windows for lower-priority routes, and batching configs. Redwood Optimize can give specific configs and we can run an experiment to see impact on cost/latency
[01:18] Ben: would quantization help? we saw mention of int8 profiles in your docs but worried about quality regression on recs
[01:26] Maya: good question, quantization (we recommend q4 or int8 for production) can cut GPU memory and cost. For rerank/recs we typically run a quality eval first; Redwood's eval harness runs offline checks, we can include your prompt set
[01:36] Aisha: we'll need that eval harness, and can share a 2k prompt sample, is that okay?
[01:40] Maya: absolutely, please send via the secure upload link, i'll put that in the follow-up email

[05:10] (discussion on cost breakout table shared in chat)
[05:15] Liam: cost drivers: longer contexts, lower cache hits, and increased concurrency. For hosted the unit price stayed stable but total spend went up 48% q/q. We modeled Dedicated vs hosted for your traffic: with Dedicated reserved capacity and moderate batching, estimated reduction in per-token cost 22-30% depending on utilization
[05:40] Priya: that 22-30% assumes 80% utilization right? we don't plan to run at 80 all the time, we need burst for marketing events
[05:48] Maya: yes the delta is utilization-sensitive; we showed a mixed policy: reserved for base, plus burst on hosted/spot — Redwood supports burst policies and automatic fallback to hosted when reserved is saturated

[09:02] Ben: quick question on p50/p95 latency numbers, last month's telemetry showed p50 at 160ms but p95 spiking to 1.2s, is that expected with your batching?
[09:13] Liam: p95 spikes align with lower cache hits and some small tail queuing during peak concurrency. We saw one incident where autoscaler went into cooldown and new nodes weren't provisioned fast enough
[09:25] Priya: yeah that's the feb 12 incident, we had an outage for about 11 minutes for the EU region which impacted our support flows
[09:33] Maya: sorry about that, from our side root cause was a misconfigured autoscale policy on the Dedicated cluster we were testing, we pushed a fix and changed the cooldown thresholds, plus added graceful degradation fallback to a lighter model family to keep requests serving while nodes spin up
[09:50] Ben: okay good, what's the SLA impact for that?
[09:53] Maya: incident fell within our internal severity banding; for customers on Dedicated with an SLA we include 99.5% uptime guarantees for region-level availability, and we log credits per our contract. we'll include the official incident report in the packet

[12:10] Aisha: procurement wants SOC 2 docs, SSO/SAML integration guide, and KMS options — can you confirm those are available?
[12:18] Maya: yes SOC2 Type II and ISO attachments are available, SAML/SSO with SCIM provisioning supported, and we have KMS/HSM integrations — I'll attach the security pack and a short integration checklist
[12:30] Priya: perfect, timeline wise procurement wants paperwork by end of next week if possible
[12:34] Maya: we'll aim for that, i'll put the security pack and contract template in the follow-up by 3/10

[15:50] (brief pause, screen share of benchmark spreadsheet)
[16:00] Liam: on Dedicated pilot: we propose a 30-day pilot with a reserved baseline sized for your 95th percentile sustained load, with burst back to hosted. Pilot scope: latency benchmarks, cost comparisons, and a production failover test. any blockers?
[16:20] Priya: main blocker is procurement signoff; also our infra team needs the architecture diagram for the VPC peering and Egress enforcement rules
[16:30] Ben: also need expected change to deployment pipeline, will we use your control plane or our private control plane? we prefer private control plane for sensitive workloads
[16:38] Maya: both supported — Redwood Private lets you run our control plane on your VPC or on-prem; for the pilot we can do customer-managed control plane in your dev VPC, that will satisfy your data residency and egress rules. we can walk through the diagram during the infra deep-dive

[19:12] Aisha: a nit — last month we saw a few hallucinations in the rerank model, flagged by our QA. any known regressions?
[19:20] Liam: could be model version change, we did roll a patched variant for the open-model in feb; we track regressions with eval sets, but we'll need the exact prompt examples to reproduce
[19:30] Maya: please send 10 failing examples, and we'll run a differential eval across the variants and follow up with recommended pinning or rollback

[22:50] (discussion about telemetry hooks)
[23:05] Ben: can we get token-level cost attribution by route? our product team wants per-route dashboards
[23:12] Maya: yes Redwood Console supports token-level breakdowns and per-route dashboards, we can enable a route tag and send dashboards to your SSO team. There's a small onboarding step to tag requests in your SDK calls

[26:40] Priya: timeline — procurement wants to close decision in two weeks, engineering wants a 30-day pilot starting asap after procurement sign-off
[26:48] Maya: noted. we'll prepare pricing scenarios (hosted vs dedicated, mixed) and send them by 3/10. Liam will set up the infra call for the week of 3/15

[30:00] (brief cross talk about sample prompts, Maya confirms secure upload link posted in chat)
[31:25] Aisha: on encryption at rest — do you support customer-managed keys for Dedicated?
[31:31] Maya: yes, both Dedicated and Private support CMK via your KMS; for hosted we offer envelope encryption with managed keys or BYOK on enterprise plans

[34:10] Ben: about fallback policies — does Redwood automatically downgrade to a smaller model family on overloads or is that a config?
[34:20] Liam: it's a policy you can enable; we ship a set of fallback rules (model variants, region fallbacks, and capacity tiers). we recommend a canary policy first and then automatic fallback for critical routes

[36:05] Priya: ok this is helpful, quick ask — can you provide an estimated savings chart for 3 scenarios: conservative (60% util), expected (75% util), and aggressive (90% util)?
[36:15] Maya: yes we'll include that in the pricing packet, plus the assumptions and sensitivity table

[38:40] (recap and next steps)
[38:50] Liam: recap: Maya will send pricing and security pack by 3/10, Liam to schedule infra deep-dive week of 3/15, Aisha to share sample prompts and traffic profile by 3/09; all owners listed in action items
[39:10] Priya: thanks all, please flag anything urgent via email, procurement timeline is tight
[39:18] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the pilot plan and the packet, appreciate the time
[39:25] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcript quality: automated transcript contained a few mis-hearings around model names (e.g., q4 -> q four, KV cache sometimes transcribed as KV cash), and a couple of speaker labels were generalized (Speaker 1). These are corrected where obvious but some minor errors remain.
